hood_desc: The futuristic waterfront showcase of the Marina Bay Sands, Gardens by the Bay, and luxury hotels, ideal for upscale travelers, sightseers, and those wanting iconic skyline views.
A vibrant heritage district of shophouses, temples, hawker food, and trendy bars, blending traditional culture with nightlife, great for foodies and history-minded visitors.
A colorful, aromatic enclave packed with Indian eateries, spice shops, and the Sri Veeramakaliamman temple, perfect for foodies and travelers seeking culture and bargains.
The premier shopping boulevard lined with malls and flagship stores, a paradise for retail lovers and those wanting a central, upscale base.
The historic Malay-Arab quarter around the Sultan Mosque, filled with boutiques, hip cafes, hookah bars, and Haji Lane's indie shops, appealing to trendy travelers and foodies.

water.note: Tap water is treated to the highest standards and safe to drink straight from the tap.

transit.pay: Simplest option: tap a contactless Visa/Mastercard or phone directly at MRT gates and on buses (SimplyGo). You can also buy a stored-value EZ-Link/SimplyGo card at station ticket offices and convenience stores (~S$10 incl. S$5 credit, ~US$7.50), or a Singapore Tourist Pass for unlimited rides.
transit.hours: MRT and buses run about 5:30am to midnight daily; after midnight, taxis and ride-hailing fill the gap.

landmarks: Marina Bay Sands
An iconic integrated resort with a ship-shaped SkyPark spanning three towers, forming Singapore's most photographed skyline silhouette.
Gardens by the Bay (Supertree Grove)
Futuristic vertical gardens up to 16 storeys tall that light up spectacularly at night, symbolizing Singapore's 'City in a Garden' vision.
Merlion Park
Home to the mythical half-lion, half-fish statue that is Singapore's national personification and most recognizable icon.
Singapore Flyer
One of the world's largest observation wheels, offering sweeping panoramic views of the Marina Bay skyline and beyond.
Raffles Hotel
A colonial-era luxury hotel and national monument famed for its white facade and as the birthplace of the Singapore Sling.
Sultan Mosque (Masjid Sultan)
The largest mosque in Singapore, its golden dome and grand facade anchor the historic Kampong Glam district.
Sri Mariamman Temple
Singapore's oldest Hindu temple, its vividly colorful gopuram tower makes it a standout photo subject in Chinatown.
Singapore Botanic Gardens
A UNESCO World Heritage Site and lush tropical garden offering a tranquil, green counterpoint to the city skyline.
Esplanade – Theatres on the Bay
A striking performing arts center nicknamed 'The Durian' for its spiky domed roofs, a distinctive Marina Bay waterfront landmark.
The Fullerton Hotel Singapore
A grand neoclassical former General Post Office turned heritage hotel, elegantly lit against the Singapore River at night.

train.note: The Shuttle Tebrau leaves from Woodlands Train Checkpoint in the north of the island (not the city centre) and crosses to JB Sentral in five minutes — book ahead, as trains sell out. There are no direct trains to Kuala Lumpur; change at JB Sentral for Malaysian ETS trains. Singapore has no domestic long-distance rail, just the MRT metro.

intl.to: Johor Bahru, Kuala Lumpur & across Malaysia

bus.note: Coaches pick up at various points around the city; everyone gets off the bus twice for immigration (Singapore exit, Malaysia entry) at the Causeway or Second Link, so keep your passport handy. Allow extra time on weekends and holidays when the border is busy.

ferry.note: Batam ferries mostly leave from HarbourFront Centre; Bintan and Desaru sailings use Tanah Merah Ferry Terminal in the east. It's an international crossing — bring your passport and arrive about an hour before departure.

half.name: Johor Bahru
half.blurb: People cross the causeway for cheap shopping, food, and Legoland just over the border.

half.name: Bintan Island
half.blurb: A quick ferry reaches white-sand beaches and resorts perfect for a relaxed seaside escape.

half.name: Batam Island
half.blurb: Visitors go for affordable spas, seafood, and beaches an easy ferry ride away.

half.name: Pulau Ubin
half.blurb: A short bumboat reaches this rustic island of old kampongs, cycling trails, and wildlife.

half.name: St John's and Lazarus Island
half.blurb: People ferry out for quiet beaches, calm lagoons, and easy swimming near the city.

half.name: Desaru Coast
half.blurb: Long sandy beaches and resorts draw those wanting a laid-back coastal day out.
